description: Every dated public step of one Robinhood Chain token in one answer, oldest first, each with the `source` it was read from. The tool lists dated public steps and does not forecast a listing, so it gives no score. A step is a lead to look into: none says why it happened, and together they do not mean an exchange will list the token. `steps` can hold BitGo's merge of the token into its lists (`custody`, with BitGo's `id` and `name` and a link to the `commit`), the contract's creation (`deploy`, given only when the transaction that first minted the token also created its contract), its first mint (`mint`, with `to`, the address that received it), the first pool on each Uniswap venue (`pool`, with `pairedWith`), the first time a market maker added one of the token's pools to its trading contracts' approved list (`pool_queued`, with the wallet as `maker`, the `venue`, the `pool`, `pairedWith`, `confirmed`, and `granted` once the addition took effect, with its own `at`, `block` and `transaction`), the first approval of the token by each wallet brainchain_market_maker_holdings follows (`approval`, with the wallet as `maker`, the `spender` and `confirmed`), and the merge that added the token's file to Trust Wallet's and MetaMask's lists (`listing`, with its `link`), dated when the list's master branch took it, not when its commit was made. Each step has `at`, `step` and `source`, and one read from the chain also has its `block` and `transaction`. Wintermute's multisig adds each pool its trading contracts may trade by queuing it on the role registry they read, and the pool can be traded from `granted` on, hours or days later. It queued Cash Cat's first pool on August 3, 2026, and its trading contract first approved the token on August 5. A `pool_queued` step's `confirmed` is true when the transaction was sent to the market maker's Safe. brainchain_custody_additions, brainchain_token_readiness, brainchain_market_maker_holdings and brainchain_token_sightings read the same steps and say what each does and does not show: an `approval` counts only when its `confirmed` is true, and anyone can create a pool for any token. Pass the token's contract address as `token`; the `contract` of an entry from brainchain_custody_additions works. `token` can also be a symbol or name, such as RLUSD or Ripple USD, looked up on BitGo's lists for Robinhood Chain; when none there goes by it, on the lists the BrainChain MCP dataset records (Trust Wallet, MetaMask, LI.FI, CoinGecko, KuCoin and Gate); and when none there does either, among every token with a Uniswap pool by the symbol its contract gives itself (`pool index`). When exactly one token goes by it, `lookup` in the answer names the `contract` it stands for and its `source`, and for one found in the dataset the `dataset` day, block and manifest read; when several do, the answer lists them as `candidates`, each with its `source`, and reads nothing more. A symbol is whatever the token's deployer chose, so check the contract before relying on one found in the pool index. To see only what was public at a point in the past, pass `atBlock`, a block number, or `at`, a time in ISO 8601 such as 2026-11-01T00:00:00Z. A step read from the chain is kept when its block is at or before that block, or the last block made at or before that time, and any other step when its time is at or before the block's time, or the time given. `until` then gives the `block` and the time (`at`) used. A `pool_queued` step whose addition took effect after the cut-off has no `granted`. BitGo's merges are read from May 11, 2026, when BitGo added its first Robinhood Chain token, so a token BitGo added at any time since has its merge, including one it has since removed. A token BitGo removed again within 16 merges, a few days at its pace, can be missed. `undated` has a listing whose merge could not be dated, with `by`, a time it had happened by, in place of `at`. With a cut-off, an undated step whose `by` is after it goes to `withheld`: it is public now, and nothing shows whether it was public by then, so it is named rather than left out. Robinhood, Bitstamp, KuCoin, Gate, LI.FI and CoinGecko publish no date for a listing, so brainchain_token_sightings reads them and they are not steps here. `deployed` says whether a contract is at the address, `token` holds its `contract` and the `name` and `symbol` it gives itself, and `unread` names a source that could not be read just now: BitGo, Trust Wallet or MetaMask. `readAt` is when the answer was made. When the BrainChain MCP dataset can be read, the pools and the followed wallets' approvals up to its head block come from it, so the chain is read only for the blocks after, and `dataset` names the day read, its `headBlock` and the SHA-256 of its `manifest`. When the dataset cannot be read, `datasetMissing` says why and every step is read live. The tool answers one request at a time, in turn with the other tools that read the chain. The first answer for a token can take half a minute; an answer that is not ready after 45 seconds says so, and asking again goes on from where it stopped. The first answer after the server starts also reads BitGo's history, with about a dozen of the 60 requests an hour GitHub allows one IP address without a key; the server keeps what it worked out, and later answers read only BitGo's changes since. If that history is not read within 45 seconds, `unread` names BitGo, and asking again goes on from where it stopped. A server whose operator set GITHUB_TOKEN reads GitHub with that token's allowance. Free, no key and no payment. Not advice.

at.description: Optional, in place of atBlock: a time in ISO 8601, such as 2026-11-01T00:00:00Z. Only the steps public by then are listed.

atBlock.description: Optional: a block number. Only the steps public by the end of that block are listed.

token.description: The token's contract address on Robinhood Chain, 0x followed by 40 hex characters, or its symbol or name, such as RLUSD.

name: brainchain_token_timeline
title: Every dated public step of a Robinhood Chain token
